subject: Arcadia Health — DPA redlines, SCCs and MSA tie-outs
messages:
From: Amelia Hart <amelia.hart@arcadiahealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Arcadia Health Legal <legal@arcadiahealth.com>, procurement@arcadiahealth.com
Date: 2026-08-30T09:12:00Z
Subject: DPA + SCCs for review — export controls / transfer impact

Jonas,

Thanks for the call yesterday. As we discussed, our legal team has one consolidated redline against the Redwood DPA focused on: (1) rejecting processor delegation for certain categories of personal data, (2) adding explicit export-control language, and (3) tightening the SCCs references to require EU-to-US transfer addenda.

We attached the redline (see Arcadia_DPA_Redline_v1.docx) and included high-level questions below:

- Can Redwood accept a limited processor-delegation carve-out for subprocessor X?
- We need evidence that tokenization/logging is disabled for health identifiers; can you provide the relevant SOC/Sys diagrams or a short statement?
- If we require an EU Transfer Impact Addendum, what are Redwood's standard controls and timelines for executing that?

We are aiming to finalize by the end of the week to hit our procurement cycle. If easiest, happy to do a quick follow-up call tomorrow morning.

Appreciate your help —
Amelia Hart
Contracts & Privacy, Arcadia Health

Attachment: Arcadia_DPA_Redline_v1.docx (document, 45KB)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Hart <amelia.hart@arcadiahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T12:05:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA + SCCs for review — export controls / transfer impact

Amelia —

Thanks for the redline and the clear asks. I'm looping in Laura (legal) and Karthik (privacy/ops) to triage the three items and come back with a consolidated proposal. Quick plan: Laura will review the DPA redline and comment inline by tomorrow EOD; Karthik will confirm evidence availability for tokenization/logging and outline the transfer controls we can commit to in an addendum. If any items require an exception or escalation, we'll flag them immediately.

Proposal: short call Thursday 09:00 BST to walk through outstanding points and confirm procurement timeline. Does that work?

Jonas Weber
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Hart <amelia.hart@arcadiahealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-31T17:10:00Z
Subject: RE: DPA + SCCs for review — Arcadia redline comments and follow-ups

Amelia / team —

Thanks for the redline. High-level response and plan below; please see the attached PDF for line-by-line comments (Redwood_DPA_Response_20260831.pdf).

1) Processor delegation: we cannot accept a blanket rejection of processor delegation across the DPA. However, we can accept a targeted carve-out: Redwood will exclude subprocessor "X-Analytics" from processing health identifiers if Arcadia provides a written list of data fields to be excluded and confirms alternative tooling. This is an operational exception that would be captured in the Order Form exhibit.

2) Export-control / transfer language: we are amenable to adding an EU Transfer Impact Addendum. Karthik will propose standard language and a control baseline (SCCs + encryption-at-rest + restricted engineer access by region). Execution timeline: we can prepare a draft addendum within 3 business days after agreement on scope.

3) Evidence & diagrams: we can provide a short attestation and a non-sensitive architecture diagram showing tokenization and log segregation for PHI. For SOC evidence, we can provide the relevant SOC/ISO summary pages and a redacted sys-diagram under NDA.

Open questions for Arcardia (please confirm):
- Which exact data fields do you classify as "health identifiers" for the carve-out? (list or sample column names works)
- Are you requesting that Redwood remove the ability for any subprocessor to see these fields, or only for selected subprocessors?

If we can get answers by EOD Wednesday, we should be positioned to produce the addendum draft and a proposed Order Form exhibit before your procurement deadline.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_DPA_Response_20260831.pdf (annotated response, 28KB)

From: Susan Klein <susan.klein@arcadiahealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Amelia Hart <amelia.hart@arcadiahealth.com>, procurement@arcadiahealth.com
Date: 2026-09-01T08:30:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA comments — follow up and clarification on fields

Laura / Jonas —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Two clarifications from our side (so your teams align properly):

• By "health identifiers" we mean the following data columns from our export schema: patient_id, nhs_number, diagnosis_code, treatment_notes (free text). We understand free text is harder — our preference is to exclude treatment_notes from processing by third-party subprocessors.

• For the subprocessor carve-out, we are asking that Redwood ensure "X-Analytics" (owned by XCorp) does not receive the treatment_notes field; other fields can be processed for analytics purposes.

We can share a sample export schema under the NDA you mentioned. Please confirm if the carve-out above is operationally viable. Procurement is aiming to sign the MSA + Order Form by next Friday.

Best,
Susan Klein
Senior Counsel — Procurement & Contracts, Arcadia Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Susan Klein <susan.klein@arcadiahealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T11:20:00Z
Subject: RE: DPA comments — operational feasibility and proposed controls

Susan / team —

Thanks for the sample scope. Short operational summary and ask:

- Excluding a specific free-text column (treatment_notes) from certain subprocessors is technically feasible if we implement a filtering step in the ingestion pipeline that strips or tokenizes that field before it reaches X-Analytics. That pipeline change would be scoped as an Order Form exhibit and would require an engineering change window (2-3 weeks) for implementation and QA.

- Proposed controls for the Transfer Impact Addendum: SCCs baseline + encryption at rest (AES-256), region-gated engineer access, monthly audit logs for access to raw payloads, and a signed attestation from Redwood's infra team. We can also run a limited, redacted sys-diagram for your security team under NDA.

Action requested from Arcadia: confirm you are comfortable with the Order Form exhibit approach (engineering change + timeline) and confirm priority so we can schedule the change window. If Arcadia needs the exclusion in place prior to contract signature, we'll need an expedited engineering commitment and an acceptance of a scoped implementation SOW.

Karthik
Director, Privacy & Product Security
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-03T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA + SCCs for review — next steps and sign-off path

Team —

Thanks all. Summary and path forward:

1) Redwood can accept the targeted subprocessor carve-out for treatment_notes for X-Analytics, implemented via an Order Form exhibit. Implementation ETA 2-3 weeks post-signature unless Arcadia wants to fund an expedited SOW.
2) Laura will finalize minor DPA language tweaks (no material concessions) and prepare the Transfer Impact Addendum draft; we expect to send both the annotated DPA and addendum by EOD Friday.
3) Karthik will provide the attestation and a redacted sys-diagram under NDA.

Amelia / Susan — please confirm by reply that you accept the Order Form exhibit route and the proposed ETA so we can lock procurement milestones. If you need faster delivery, indicate budget for an expedited SOW and we'll route to operations.

Jonas Weber
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
